quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person in charge of the whole school!
quests.question: Principal
quests.hint: This person leads the whole school, not just one classroom.
quests.explanation: That's right! A principal helps every teacher and student in the school.
quests.funFact: A principal often visits many classrooms in just one single school day!

quests.instruction: Touch the item we open to read words and look at pictures!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: You open it and turn each page to find out what happens next.
quests.explanation: Well done! A book can teach us new things or tell a fun story.
quests.funFact: The very first books were written by hand, long before printing was invented!

quests.instruction: Touch the small tool that rubs pencil marks away from your paper!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: It never works on pen marks, only on pencil marks.
quests.explanation: Well done! An eraser helps keep your paper neat and tidy.
quests.funFact: Erasers are made from rubber, which is why they can bend and squish!

quests.instruction: Touch the item that needs a paintbrush before it goes onto paper!
quests.question: Paint
quests.hint: It is wet and colorful until it dries on your paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! Paint is the colorful liquid we brush onto paper for art.
quests.funFact: Paint dries as the water inside it slowly disappears into the air!

quests.instruction: Find the tool that snips paper into new shapes when you squeeze it!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: It has two blades that open and close like a little mouth.
quests.explanation: That's right! We squeeze the handles of scissors to cut along a line.
quests.funFact: School scissors often have rounded tips to help keep little fingers safe!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we use to color a picture, not to write words!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: You press it on paper to fill a picture with color, not words.
quests.explanation: Well done! Crayons come in many colors so every picture can look different.
quests.funFact: One box of crayons can have more than sixty different colors inside!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the room where students eat their lunch!
quests.question: Cafeteria
quests.hint: This big room has many tables where students sit to eat.
quests.explanation: That's right! We carry our lunch trays into the cafeteria to eat.
quests.funFact: Some school cafeterias can serve lunch to hundreds of hungry students every day!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the room where you sit and learn each day!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: This room has desks, chairs, and a board at the front.
quests.explanation: Yes! A classroom is the room where you learn together with your teacher.
quests.funFact: Classrooms around the world can look very different, but they are all places to learn!

quests.instruction: Touch the container that keeps us feeling cool and refreshed in class!
quests.question: Water Bottle
quests.hint: It is filled with water and often kept in your backpack.
quests.explanation: Yes! A water bottle holds water so we can drink during the school day.
quests.funFact: Drinking enough water can help your brain stay focused during class!

quests.instruction: Touch the school tool we use to write letters and draw pictures!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: It leaves a soft grey line when it touches your page.
quests.explanation: Well done! A pencil makes marks that an eraser can rub away later.
quests.funFact: The soft grey part inside a pencil is called graphite, not lead at all!

quests.instruction: Touch the straight tool we lay flat on paper before drawing a line!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: You press it flat on your paper before drawing a line.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a ruler when we need a perfectly straight line.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people used their own feet and hands to measure things before rulers!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the room where a caring adult answers the school phone!
quests.question: Office
quests.hint: This room often has a phone and helpers who greet everyone.
quests.explanation: Yes! The office is where visitors check in and school helpers do their work.
quests.funFact: The school office often keeps important papers safe for every single student!

quests.instruction: Find the board at the front of class that markers wipe clean off of!
quests.question: Whiteboard
quests.hint: It is smooth, shiny, and usually white in color.
quests.explanation: Well done! A whiteboard helps the whole class see the lesson clearly.
quests.funFact: Some whiteboards are magnetic, so little magnets can stick to them too!

quests.instruction: Find the seat with four legs that we sit on in class!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: It usually has four legs, a seat, and a back to lean on.
quests.explanation: That's right! We sit on a chair while we work at our desk.
quests.funFact: Some classroom chairs are stacked together and stored when they're not needed!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool with a handle and soft hairs used for painting!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: It has a long handle and soft bristles on one end.
quests.explanation: Yes! A paintbrush spreads paint smoothly across our paper.
quests.funFact: Paintbrush bristles can be made from soft animal hair or from nylon!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for a friend who learns in your class with you!
quests.question: Classmate
quests.hint: This person sits near you and learns in the very same class.
quests.explanation: That's right! A classmate shares lessons, games, and school days with you.
quests.funFact: Working with a classmate on a project is a great way to learn together!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person who takes care of the library!
quests.question: Librarian
quests.hint: This person knows exactly where every book belongs on its shelf.
quests.explanation: That's right! A librarian can help you pick a great book to read.
quests.funFact: A librarian often knows hundreds of book titles and where each one belongs!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin, flat sheet that we write and draw on every day!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: You can fold it, cut it, or draw on it in class.
quests.explanation: Well done! Paper is ready for a pencil, crayon, or marker to color it.
quests.funFact: Paper was first made from tree bark, plants, and old cloth long ago!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool teachers often use to write big words on a board!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: Its ink is thick and bold, much darker than a pencil's line.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a marker for bright writing and drawing.
quests.funFact: Some markers even smell like fruit, such as strawberry or grape!

quests.instruction: Point to the person who answers your questions and checks your work!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: You raise your hand when you have a question for this person.
quests.explanation: That's right! A teacher explains new lessons and answers our questions.
quests.funFact: A single teacher can help hundreds of students learn over many years!

quests.instruction: Touch the bag that lives inside our backpack, full of writing tools!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It is small enough to fit right inside your backpack.
quests.explanation: Well done! A pencil case keeps our desk neat and organized.
quests.funFact: Some pencil cases can stand up on their own like a little box!

quests.instruction: Find the piece of furniture where we write and stack our books!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: It is flat on top, just the right size to hold your books.
quests.explanation: That's right! We keep our books and pencils on our desk in class.
quests.funFact: The word desk comes from an old word meaning a table for writing!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the helper who gently checks if you are feeling better!
quests.question: School Nurse
quests.hint: This person often has bandages ready to help with a small scrape.
quests.explanation: Yes! A school nurse takes care of students who feel unwell or get hurt.
quests.funFact: A school nurse often keeps a cozy cot ready for students who need a short rest!

quests.instruction: Find the item we fill with our own writing and drawings!
quests.question: Notebook
quests.hint: Its pages start out empty until you fill them with your writing.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a notebook to practice writing and take notes.
quests.funFact: Writing in a notebook every day is a great way to practice new words!

quests.instruction: Find the object we check to see if it's almost time for recess!
quests.question: Clock
quests.hint: Its hands move all day, even when nobody is watching.
quests.explanation: Well done! A clock helps our whole class know when it's time to go.
quests.funFact: Some classroom clocks have a big hand for minutes and a small hand for hours!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the big yellow vehicle that takes us to school!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It is big, often yellow, and has many seats inside.
quests.explanation: That's right! We ride a school bus to get to school safely.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the quiet room filled with rows of books!
quests.question: Library
quests.hint: This room is filled with shelf after shelf of books to borrow.
quests.explanation: That's right! We visit a library to find a new book to read.
quests.funFact: A library can hold thousands of books for students to borrow and enjoy!

quests.instruction: Point to the box we carry to school full of yummy food!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: It keeps your food safe on the way to school.
quests.explanation: That's right! We open a lunchbox at lunchtime to enjoy our food.
quests.funFact: Packing your own lunchbox can be a fun way to choose your favorite foods!

quests.instruction: Touch the item that closes like a book to protect our papers!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It opens and closes like a thin book made of paper or plastic.
quests.explanation: Yes! A folder holds loose papers safely so they do not get lost or bent.
quests.funFact: Some folders have pockets on both sides to sort different papers!

quests.instruction: Touch the item a teacher uses to write big words on a board!
quests.question: Chalk
quests.hint: It writes on a hard, dark board instead of on paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! Chalk is the stick we use to write on a blackboard.
quests.funFact: Chalk is made from a soft rock that can be ground into a stick!
